justifications.c1: Per-impact cost is vendor-only and inconsistent (FleetRabbit '$10,000 average' vs '$200–800'; Dexory title only); the one independent UK figure (Bingley collapse, £157,500 fines, search-confirmed) arose from load-testing, not an unreported impact, and no UK upright replacement price was found.
justifications.c2: HSG76 weekly PRRS visual checks recur at every site (Warehouse News, Bureau Veritas), but impact frequency rests on unsourced vendor claims (FleetRabbit 8–12 unreported per reported, search-confirmed as vendor marketing citing no study; SafetyNow 90–95%), and the sensor supplements rather than replaces the weekly check.
justifications.c3: Weekly PRRS checks and annual paid SARI inspections (Bureau Veritas) are documented with frequency, but no labour or £ cost (Mazzella says 'depends on size'), and the sensor removes neither.
justifications.c4: HSG76 PRRS role with weekly checks and recording, SEMA red/amber/green with a 4-week amber-to-red rule, annual SARI inspection, and HSE racking-collapse prosecutions (2026 Bingley, 2013 Corby); none of the enforcement turns on unreported impact damage, and HSG76 is guidance cited only via trade summaries.
justifications.c5: The PRRS is a named in-house role in HSG76 and SARI inspections are a budget line, but no job advert or role description shows PRRS or warehouse manager budget authority for monitoring.
justifications.c6: SARI inspectors visit annually and racking-repair firms visit after damage, and rack-protector supplier A-SAFE already bundles RackEye sensors with guards; that bundler is a competitor rather than an available channel, and no SARI firm is shown selling tech.
justifications.c7: Proven but crowded: A-SAFE RackEye (search-confirmed: SMS alerts, cloud dashboard, leased turnkey), Rack Sense, a European real-time rack monitor, Fraunhofer crash sensor, Linde truck-side sensor, drone/robot inspection; no prices and no evidenced gap.
justifications.c8: Off-the-shelf EM320-TILT is €74.90–83 per node with 3–5 yr battery, but it is a tilt sensor not documented for shock detection (custom firmware needed), damage-vs-nuisance discrimination is the incumbent's patented core, and per-upright cost scales badly across a DC.
justifications.c9: Weekly checks, 4-week amber deadlines and annual SARI recur, and RackEye is sold as a leased cloud service, but no subscription price is evidenced.
justifications.c10: HSE press release and British Safety Council on collapses, trade press (Logistics Matters), Canadian employment rulings on unreported impacts, and viral collapse coverage; the unreported-impact problem itself is mainly evidenced by vendors.

weakest: Crowded, unpriced competition: A-SAFE RackEye already delivers the same concept (rack-mounted impact sensors, SMS alerts, cloud, leasing) through its barrier channel, and no gap is evidenced.
